name: Oludeniz Beach Village and the Blue Lagoon
tagline: Postcard beach at the heart of it all
description: The main village strung along the famous Blue Flag beach and the calm turquoise Blue Lagoon inside the nature park. Walkable and scenic, it is the paragliding landing zone and boat-trip hub, packed with beachfront hotels, cafes, and tour operators through the warm season.
bestFor: Beach lovers and adventure slow-travellers who want the lagoon on their doorstep
pros: Steps from the Blue Lagoon and Blue Flag beach
cons: Busiest and priciest in peak summer
Very quiet and largely closed in winter

name: Hisaronu
tagline: The lively resort strip on the hill
description: A built-up resort town on the hillside above Oludeniz, packed with hotels, bars, restaurants, and shops. It is the liveliest base for nightlife and budget accommodation, with frequent dolmus links down to the beach and up toward Babadag, though it lacks the beachfront setting.
bestFor: Budget stays and travellers wanting bars, restaurants, and buzz
pros: Easy dolmus links to beach and Babadag

name: Ovacik
tagline: Quieter valley base near the action
description: A calmer, greener valley area just inland from Hisaronu, with villas, apartments, and a more residential feel. It suits longer, slower stays away from the crowds while keeping the beach, bars, and Babadag shuttles a short dolmus or drive away.
bestFor: Longer slow-travel stays wanting quiet and value near the resorts
pros: Quieter and greener than the resort strips
Short hop to Hisaronu and the beach
cons: Relies on dolmus or a car to get around

name: Fethiye
tagline: The larger town, marina, and services
description: The bustling town roughly 20 minutes away by dolmus, with a marina, harbour, lively markets, and far more year-round services. It has the fullest local life, better long-stay rentals, more cafes, and a small but growing remote-worker presence, making it the practical base beyond the resort.
vibe: Working town, marina buzz, year-round life
bestFor: Remote workers and long-stayers wanting services, community, and year-round options
pros: More services, cafes, and year-round rentals
Marina, markets, and real local life
cons: Busier and more urban than the resort villages
